guardrails.title: AI Assistant content safety (OpenAI omni-moderation)
guardrails.scope: Only applies to the AI Assistant feature: before requests are sent upstream, LiteLLM Proxy calls OpenAI omni-moderation to screen user input. Flagged requests are blocked early to reduce upstream policy risk/bans.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.body: The API attaches guardrail names (e.g. openai-moderation-pre) to each Assistant request. LiteLLM Proxy runs these checks in pre_call and blocks unsafe inputs before calling the upstream LLM.

setup.title: Setup
setup.proxyConfigSuffix: This repo already includes the OpenAI moderation guardrail (requires OPENAI_API_KEY):
setup.apiEnvSuffix: (comma-separate to add more guardrail names if needed)
setup.verify: 3) Verify: in the AI Assistant page, try an obviously malicious/violating prompt. It should be blocked with a friendly message and will not call the upstream LLM.

guardrails.notes: Cost: OpenAI omni-moderation is typically not billed separately (check OpenAI’s latest policy). It adds a small latency overhead. By default we only screen inputs (pre_call). If you also want to screen outputs, add openai-moderation-post to ASSISTANT_GUARDRAILS.

hint.title: Guardrails are enforced via LiteLLM Proxy
hint.body: Enable/disable moderation guardrails for the AI assistant. Make sure the LiteLLM Proxy config defines the required guardrails.

docs.scope: This setting ONLY affects the AI Assistant page (/assistant). Other features using LiteLlmService (news pipeline / analysis / monitoring) do not pass guardrails, so they are NOT moderated by this switch.
docs.setupBody:
1) Configure LiteLLM Proxy guardrails in infra/litellm/litellm-config.yaml (openai-moderation-pre / openai-moderation-post).
2) In this panel, save OpenAI API keys (stored in MySQL).
3) Set LITELLM_CONFIG_INTERNAL_TOKEN in both API and litellm env (root .env or infra/docker/.env) so litellm can fetch keys on startup, then restart the litellm service.
4) (Optional) In this panel, enable output moderation if you also want to moderate assistant responses (may impact streaming).

openaiKeys.description: These keys are stored in MySQL and fetched by LiteLLM Proxy at startup (requires LITELLM_CONFIG_INTERNAL_TOKEN), used for OpenAI model calls and omni-moderation guardrails. If you provide multiple keys, assistant moderation calls are spread across them. Restart the litellm service after updating.

notice.title: Translation API (DeepLX)
notice.body: Translate to Simplified Chinese uses DeepLX as primary and can fall back to a backup translation endpoint. If both requests fail, the page keeps original text and shows a translation error tag.

hints.translationApiKey: Leave empty to keep current key. Stored encrypted when secret encryption is enabled in system security settings.
hints.translationFallbackApiEnabled: When enabled, the system automatically retries translation with the fallback endpoint after DeepLX fails.

hints.finnhubApiKey: Used for indices/sectors/commodities. Leave empty to keep current key. Stored encrypted when secret encryption is enabled.
hints.fredApiKey: Used for Fed indicators and balance sheet data. Leave empty to keep current key. Stored encrypted when secret encryption is enabled.
hints.translationApiMaxRetries: Maximum retry count after translation request failures.

runtimeGuide.title: Headed mode and Xvfb
runtimeGuide.noAutoBootstrap: This console only provides guidance and does not auto-start Xvfb for you.
runtimeGuide.principleBody: When headless=false, Chromium needs a display server. Xvfb provides a virtual X11 display (for example :99) so headed rendering can run in containers without a physical monitor.
runtimeGuide.step1: Prefer Headless for routine crawls, and use Headed only when anti-bot scenarios need it.
runtimeGuide.step2: When using Headed, ensure Xvfb/DISPLAY are configured in the crawl4ai container.
runtimeGuide.step3: If display errors persist, switch this task back to Headless first, then verify container env settings.
runtimeGuide.displayIssueHint: Headed runtime failed because DISPLAY/Xvfb is unavailable. Enable Xvfb in crawl4ai or switch this task to Headless.
runtimeGuide.timeoutIssueHint: Display may be ready, but browser startup/navigation timed out. Check crawl4ai load and task timeout settings.

virtualScroll.title: Virtual scroll
virtualScroll.description: Bounded scrolling for infinite-scroll or virtualized lists. Use it when content loads as you scroll (feeds, timelines, lazy lists).
virtualScroll.containerSelectorHint: CSS selector of the scrollable container. Use "body" for full page scrolling.
